claims.statement: Polish government guidance says economic operators have had to ensure digital accessibility from 28 June 2025 under the Polish Accessibility Act, which implements the European Accessibility Act.
The Polish guidance describes e-commerce broadly as online consumer contracting for products or services and explicitly exempts microenterprises providing services.

Covered e-commerce providers must publish accessible information about how the service meets requirements and notify the Minister of Digital Affairs when the service does not comply, including planned corrective action or a claimed exception.

contrary_evidence: Microenterprises providing services are exempt, removing many small online shops from the direct buyer pool.
Free scanners and agency audits are widely substitutable for basic automated detection.
Automated checks cannot establish full accessibility compliance and can create false confidence.

economics.acquisition_route: Per-portfolio agency resale, CMS marketplace listings, and fixed-price baseline scans for covered merchants
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 2,000 storefronts at PLN 6,000 annual recurring revenue yields PLN 12m revenue before audits; at a 40% operating margin, cumulative distributions over seven to nine years could build roughly PLN 20m founder net worth
economics.founder_time: Three hours per day for automation and issue triage, with expert manual reviews scheduled and subcontracted rather than handled ad hoc
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automated release checks and evidence storage can exceed 85% gross margin; manual spot checks lower the blended target to about 70%-75%
economics.payback: Target under three months because setup fees pay for baseline mapping and agency commission
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 2,000-8,000 baseline setup and PLN 300-1,200 per storefront per month, with expert remediation quoted separately by partners
economics.retention_or_repeat: Themes, checkout flows, plugins, and content change frequently, so regression monitoring repeats monthly if the product catches issues before complaints

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A labelled corpus of recurring accessibility defects and verified fixes at the theme, component, checkout, and CMS-plugin level
fingerprint.customer: Polish e-commerce service providers above microenterprise status and WooCommerce or custom-web agencies managing portfolios of such consumer storefronts
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Polish web agencies, commerce-platform extensions, and accessibility specialists resell the release gate across existing merchant portfolios
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: CI and URL-based testing, CMS-component issue clustering, annotated remediation tickets, accessible disclosure generation, and versioned evidence, with optional expert spot checks; per-site setup and subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A web agency or merchant pays for a baseline assessment when a site enters coverage, then pays per storefront each month when deployments are scanned and evidence is refreshed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The Polish Accessibility Act has applied since 28 June 2025 to covered e-commerce services, requiring digital accessibility, public information on how the service meets requirements, and regulator notification when identified gaps are being remediated

founder_fit: Automated testing, defect clustering, and regression analytics fit data and software skills
Agency resale offers portfolio acquisition without a founder brand or frequent individual sales calls
A single storefront can test demand with limited capital and reversible effort
Recurring scans and evidence archives form a scalable product rather than a pure audit consultancy
risks: Marketing the product as certification rather than evidence support could create legal liability.
A crawler may miss authenticated checkout and dynamic-component barriers.
Agency partners may clone the workflow or bundle it at no incremental price.
Manual remediation demand could overwhelm the intended product model.

structure.commercial_archetype: Compliance release-gate SaaS with partner-delivered remediation
structure.control_point: The deployment check that prevents a storefront release from silently degrading its accessibility evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Meaningful human-verifiable coverage beyond automated scans and correct identification of merchants outside the microenterprise exemption

thesis: A continuous accessibility release gate for Polish e-commerce services above the microenterprise exemption can combine automated checks, CMS-specific remediation tickets, public accessibility information, and a defensible evidence archive. The product should sell through agencies per managed storefront and explicitly avoid one-click overlay claims; recurring value comes from catching regressions every time a theme, checkout, or campaign changes.
title: PAD Release Gate for Polish E-Commerce
uncertainties: The number of covered Polish storefronts not already served by an agency accessibility process is unknown.
Merchants' willingness to pay monthly after a one-time remediation has not been tested.
No evidence validates agency resale economics or the 2,000-storefront wealth scenario.
The minimum defensible frequency and scope of expert manual checks require accessibility-specialist input.
